evidence.quote: # Demo server: https://ha-mcp-demo-server.qc-h.net (login: mcp/mcp, resets weekly)

reason: A working long-lived Home Assistant token is committed on purpose for the public demo server (which also publishes mcp/mcp login and resets weekly). It grants nothing beyond the public demo, but anyone can drive that demo instance with it.
fix: Keep it only if the demo instance is meant to be public and isolated; otherwise remove it, rotate the token and fetch demo credentials at runtime.

evidence.quote: Always run this before ha_restart() to ensure configuration is valid.

reason: Safety guidance: validate config before restarting. It names another tool only to make the user's restart safer.
Test fixture token for the throw-away Home Assistant container used in CI (the file says so and points to the bundled test auth store); it does not unlock a real instance.

The add-on (host_network) serves MCP over plain HTTP on all interfaces with the Supervisor token behind it; the only protection is an unguessable URL path. The auto path has 128-bit entropy, but it is printed to the add-on log, sent in clear text on the LAN, and a user-chosen custom path is accepted with no strength check.
fix: Require a bearer token (or HA auth) on the endpoint instead of a URL secret, enforce a minimum length/entropy for custom secret_path, avoid logging the full path, and recommend TLS / binding to the HA ingress network only.

reason: Only a relative path is built and sent through the client configured with the Home Assistant base URL; the host cannot be changed, so this is not SSRF. At most a crafted entity_id reaches another GET endpoint of the same HA API that other tools already expose.
card_type is checked against a bundled allowlist and appended to a fixed raw.githubusercontent.com base; the host cannot be chosen.
The release URL must match a github.com pattern and only owner/repo/tag (no slashes) are placed into a fixed api.github.com URL; no internal host is reachable.
Fixed host raw.githubusercontent.com with segments taken from a regex that excludes '/'; not SSRF.
Fixed host and repo (api.github.com/home-assistant/core); only the tag varies, so no internal service can be reached.
Fixed public host raw.githubusercontent.com; domain only changes the path on GitHub's CDN, so this cannot reach internal services.

title: OAuth mode accepts unsigned, self-made bearer tokens and connects to the ha_url inside them (auth bypass + SSRF)
reason: verify_token only base64-decodes JSON; there is no signature, expiry or check that the server issued it. Anyone can send Authorization: Bearer base64({"ha_url":"http://169.254.169.254","ha_token":"x"}) and every tool call makes the server send requests to that URL (internal services, the host's localhost) and return the responses. Tokens also carry the user's HA long-lived token in readable form and never expire.
fix: Issue opaque random tokens (or signed+encrypted JWTs with exp and audience) and keep HA credentials server-side keyed by token; reject tokens the server did not issue; validate ha_url at consent time against an allowlist / block private and link-local ranges.

title: HTTP/SSE modes bind 0.0.0.0 on a default '/mcp' path with no authentication
reason: main_web/main_sse run with the operator's HOMEASSISTANT_TOKEN from the environment, listen on every interface, and the default path is the well-known /mcp with no auth. Anyone on the network can call all tools (unlock doors, call any service, install HACS code).
fix: Default to 127.0.0.1, refuse to start on a public interface without a bearer token or a generated high-entropy secret path, and validate Origin/Host.

title: Model-written Python executed with exec() behind an AST filter
reason: python_transform is executed in the server process; the guard is an AST allowlist plus empty __builtins__, which the review guide rates as insufficient. I found no escape in the allowed node set (dunders and getattr are blocked), but While loops and list multiplication are allowed, so `while True: pass` or `x=[0]*10**10` hangs or exhausts the server (sync exec inside the async handler).
fix: Replace exec with a declarative patch format (JSON Patch / jq, already supported), or run the transform in a separate process with CPU/memory/time limits.

title: HACS add-repository + download lets any tool caller install arbitrary code into Home Assistant
reason: A prompt-injected model can add an attacker's GitHub repo as a custom integration, download it and restart HA (ha_restart exists); custom integrations are Python that runs inside Home Assistant with full access. The only control is the advisory destructiveHint annotation; these tools load by default.
fix: Disable HACS write tools by default behind an explicit opt-in flag, require out-of-band human confirmation (MCP elicitation) for add/download/restart, and optionally restrict to an allowlist of repositories.

title: File-write tool can publish arbitrary HTML/JS under www/ (served on the HA origin)
reason: Path containment is checked (normpath + resolve, though with a prefix startswith), but www/ is served at /local/ on the Home Assistant origin, so an injected write of www/x.html with script can steal the HA session of whoever opens it. Feature is off by default (HAMCP_ENABLE_FILESYSTEM_TOOLS); impact depends on whether you enable it.
fix: Keep the flag off unless needed, require confirmation for writes, block .html/.js/.svg in www/, and use Path.is_relative_to for containment.

title: Third-party release notes and docs returned to the model unmarked
reason: Release notes of any installed HACS/custom repo (author-controlled text) go straight into the model context of an agent that can also call services and install code (M004), giving a path for injected instructions.
fix: Mark returned notes as untrusted data and keep high-impact tools behind confirmation.
